newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Washington's Barry pushes trade, tourism in Seoul.
newsitem.headline: Washington's Barry pushes trade, tourism in Seoul.

text.p: Washington D.C. mayor Marion Barry is in Seoul to promote trade and tourism to the U.S. capital, the United States embassy said on Thursday.
"He's in town to discuss trade and tourism into Washington," said press attache Patrick Linehan.
Barry was not available to comment on his trip.
During the November 12-15 visit to South Korea, his 14-member public and private sector delegation planned to meet government and business officials, a press statement from Barry's office said.
Washington D.C. is virtually bankrupt. The financial management of the district was taken over in February 1995 by a federal control board.
Barry, a civil rights leader and liberal Democrat, is one of America's more controversial black politicians.
The son of a sharecropper, he joined the civil rights movement in the 60's to protest segregation. He was elected mayor of Washington D.C. for the first time in 1978.
Barry has made no secret of his problems with alcohol and served time in prison in 1990 on a federal drug charge.
He overcame the publicity surrounding his arrest, trial and conviction to be re-elected in 1994 to a fourth term.
Barry's delegation will leave for China on November 15.
